answer_sql:
WITH agg AS (
  SELECT
    'customer' AS reading,
    dc.country_name AS country,
    SUM(l.net_amount) AS net_revenue
  FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS l
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_customer AS cu
    ON l.customer_key = cu.customer_key
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_country AS dc
    ON cu.country_code = dc.country_code
  WHERE
    dc.country_code <> '--'
  GROUP BY
    1,
    2
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    'store',
    dc.country_name,
    SUM(l.net_amount)
  FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS l
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_store AS s
    ON l.store_key = s.store_key
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_country AS dc
    ON s.country_code = dc.country_code
  WHERE
    dc.country_code <> '--'
  GROUP BY
    1,
    2
), ranked AS (
  SELECT
    reading,
    country,
    net_revenue,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY reading ORDER BY net_revenue DESC) AS rnk
  FROM agg
)
SELECT
  reading,
  country,
  net_revenue
FROM ranked
WHERE
  rnk <= 5
ORDER BY
  reading,
  net_revenue DESC

body.value: The ten rows returned are the five highest-earning countries under each reading of "country", with net revenue — money customers were actually charged, after discount, in USD — accumulated over every sale Contoso recorded from 2016-05-18 to 2025-12-31. One row is one country under one reading. The five `customer` rows attribute each sale to where its buyer lives and between them account for all 223,974 sales lines and the whole 218,814,471.66. The five `store` rows attribute each sale to where the selling shop trades; they cover 130,424 lines and 132,024,417.53 and leave out 93,550 web-shop lines worth 86,790,054.13, which have no country to be attributed to. Every figure matches what steps 3 and 4 measured. NOT INCLUDED in either list: the `--` sentinel, a placeholder and not a place; any returns, refunds, tax or shipping, none of which this data records; and any currency conversion — the amounts are already USD.

value:
Which country do you mean — the country the CUSTOMER lives in, or the country the SHOP that made the sale stands in? Both are proper answers and I am not allowed to pick for you, because they differ by 87 million dollars.

(a) WHERE THE BUYER LIVES — places every sale, web orders included, 218,814,471.66 in total:
  1. United States — 111,862,187.56
  2. Germany — 24,638,830.18
  3. Canada — 23,242,027.53
  4. United Kingdom — 23,049,533.37
  5. Australia — 13,360,672.61

(b) WHERE THE SELLING SHOP TRADES — physical shops only, 132,024,417.53. The web shop's 86,790,054.13, two fifths of all the money Contoso has taken, belongs to no country under this reading and is absent from the list entirely:
  1. United States — 67,827,886.26
  2. United Kingdom — 15,058,669.67
  3. Germany — 14,382,768.44
  4. Canada — 13,712,923.81
  5. Australia — 7,501,114.89

WHAT YOUR CHOICE DOES NOT CHANGE: the five countries are the same either way — United States, Germany, Canada, United Kingdom, Australia — and so are the two ends of the list, the United States first and Australia fifth. The Netherlands is sixth under both readings and not close to getting in, 42% and 44% below fifth place, so no plausible reading of the question admits a different country. What the choice DOES change is the three places in the middle — Germany, Canada, UK becomes UK, Germany, Canada — and every figure, each one roughly 40% lower under (b). A third reading, the country of the shop's SITE rather than the shop, is also declared; I priced it and it matches (b) to the cent on all eight countries, so it is not a separate option.

Both lists cover all ten years on record, 2016-05-18 to 2025-12-31, and both exclude the `--` sentinel, which is not a country.

Two populations, one per reading, both drawn from all 223,974 sales lines over the full recorded extent of order_date, 2016-05-18 to 2025-12-31, with no channel filter at the base — store.resolution.the_channel_is_the_location_sentinel scopes its `physical` default with `applies: subject` and the subject here is a measure, and the operator's ruling of 2026-10-18 puts unqualified revenue at 218,814,471.66 across both channels. The CUSTOMER list is computed over all 223,974 lines and all 218,814,471.66, because every customer carries a real country. The STORE list is computed over only the 130,424 lines and 132,024,417.53 taken in physical shops: the web shop's country is the `--` sentinel, and country.exclusion.sentinel_is_not_a_country (default population `real`) keeps it out of any list of countries, so 93,550 lines worth 86,790,054.13 fall outside that population entirely. Both exclude `--`. Nothing else is excluded — no country, customer, store or product was dropped, and no country was omitted for being small; there are simply eight, of which these are the top five.

The decomposition's own note — 'the country associated with the sale as the business normally reports it (customer/billing country)' — is exactly the silent assumption this rule exists to prevent, and taking it would have hidden an 87 million dollar difference behind a list that looks complete.
